newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended steady to higher on Friday, after technical buying by local investors following Thursday's price plunges, traders said.
Prices were unchanged to 150 yen higher, and the benchmark May 1998 contract was up 100 yen at 14,900 yen a tonne.

The market opened mixed, as local investors could not determine a clear direction, traders said. "Investors assumed price losses yesterday were too much, and generated technical buying from late morning," a brokerage house trader said.
Price gains in CBOT overnight corn trading also encouraged investors to buy, treaders said.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.88 per bushel at 0710 GMT, unchanged from the Thursday close.
The spot May soybean futures contract on the overnight trading system was at $8.89-3/4 at 0710 GMT, up from $8.87-1/2 at Thursday's close.
